title: Distance-Hiding Fingerprints for Text Embeddings via Secure SimHash

contributions.purpose: Characterize the privacy leakage in binary LSH fingerprints.
contributions.mechanism: Formalizes the privacy-utility tradeoff for binary fingerprints and identifies the SimHash collision probability curve P(s)=(1+s)/2 as the root cause of pairwise-distance leakage.
contributions.evaluation: Analytical characterization; no numeric metric (framing/formalization contribution).
contributions.domain: Privacy-preserving similarity search over text-embedding fingerprints.
contributions.source_quote: We formalize the privacy-utility tradeoff for binary fingerprints and identify the collision probability curve as the root cause of distance leakage.

contributions.purpose: Provide a fingerprint transform that hides distances while keeping utility.
contributions.mechanism: Secure SimHash composes k independent SimHash bits with XOR so the collision probability becomes P_sec(s)=1/2+1/2*p(s)^k, flattening curves for non-neighbors while preserving near-neighbor detection, with supporting theoretical analysis.
contributions.evaluation: Collision probability approaches 0.5 for low-similarity pairs as k increases, making distance estimation uninformative; ablation attributes gains to XOR composition, not reduced bit count.
contributions.domain: Privacy-preserving similarity search over text-embedding fingerprints.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Secure SimHash with theoretical analysis showing how k-composition with XOR flattens collision curves for non-neighbors while preserving near-neighbor detection.

contributions.mechanism: Evaluates Secure SimHash on BEIR Quora against randomized response and noise injection baselines on the privacy-utility Pareto frontier.
contributions.evaluation: Dominates the Pareto frontier: AUC@0.5=0.463 (near random-guess) at Recall@10=0.780, significantly outperforming baselines.
contributions.domain: Privacy-preserving similarity search over text-embedding fingerprints.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate empirically on BEIR Quora that Secure SimHash dominates the privacy-utility Pareto frontier, achieving AUC@0.5=0.463 (near random-guess) at Recall@10=0.780, significantly outperforming randomized response and noise injection baselines.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Riazi et al. (2016) proposed secure binary embeddings using probabilistic transformations over LSH families, providing information-theoretic privacy bounds against triangulation attacks... However, these approaches either require expensive cryptographic computation or provide privacy guarantees that may not directly address the distance-hiding problem in binary fingerprints.

However, as we demonstrate empirically, randomized response approaches face a fundamental tradeoff: achieving strong privacy requires extreme randomization that destroys utility. Our work addresses this limitation by proposing a mechanism that flattens collision probability curves rather than adding noise, enabling better privacy-utility tradeoffs.
